statusNote: DRAFT AWAITING MAX'S GREENLIGHT — do NOT build against this yet. Scoped 2026-07-28 off the grounding at evidence/GROUNDING-2026-07-28.md (36 agents: 5 lenses, adversarial refute-by-default on every finding, synthesis; 14 findings refuted or corrected). The grounding's verdict on the fix AS THE HANDOFF PROPOSED IT was NEEDS-FIX, for two reasons; this contract resolves one and declares the other a non-goal. (1) RESOLVED HERE: the proposed edit was ungated, and shipping ^1.70 unconditionally would fix super-Earths by breaking Mars, Mercury, Europa and Titan — at Mars (R_c=0.53) the pure ratio power is 56% above the piecewise form at R=4. Hence the composition gate and the piecewise-in-absolute-R form, both recorded in designDecisions. (2) DECLARED A NON-GOAL: the global relief-amplitude uniform uPerturb does not read this field at all — it is fed the canonical, radius-blind u.surfaceGravity (planet-lod-lab.html:3016 <- planet-lod-lab-core.js:609-611), and reliefEnvelope discards its radiusEarth argument outright (planet-lod-lab-core.js:1103-1105). This directly contradicts the comment at planet-lod-lab-core.js:1090-1093 that justified dropping the explicit 1/RE term on the grounds that 'g ALREADY carries the radius signal'. At the live wiring it carries nothing. Same family as the census's frozen-_fp finding and Max's own R1-ship observation (a) about legacy shader systems not being wired to procgen. Filed as a finding, NOT fixed here, because the handoff is explicit that the gravity fix goes 'first and alone'. THE THIRD CITATION IS NOW CLOSED: Valencia+2006 (astro-ph/0511150) was retrieved during grounding; its Table 2 puts the SUB-Earth exponent near 1.30 (five fitted beta -> n = 1.27-1.34), NOT the 1.0 incompressible asymptote the handoff implicitly assumed — so the low branch is 4/3, not 1. Separately, Melosh 2011 ch.3 and Kite+2009 were retrieved and read in full (research/superearth-relief-law-citations-resolved-2026-07-28.md); they bear on the v2 relief derivation, not on this workstream, EXCEPT that Melosh independently confirms h = 2Y/(rho_c g) is his eq 3.17 rearranged.
designDecisions: COMPOSITION GATE = three-way via compositionClass (e1Regime.js:67), NOT ungated and NOT an h2-he-only gate. Taken WITHOUT asking Max, per feedback_physics-first-worldengine-scoping (physics-derivable questions are working-Claude's, not interview forks). Zeng+2016 is a rocky two-layer PREM fit valid 1-8 M_E and CMF 0.0-0.4; it has no standing for the 5 h2-he presets (Jovian 11.2, Hot Jupiter 13.0, Saturnian 9.4, Neptunian 3.9, Sub-Neptune 2.7) NOR for the 4 icy ones (Titan 0.4, Frozen 0.5, Europa 0.5, Crystal 0.8), whose ice EOS is a different family. Measured evidence against the ungated form: fitting dln g/dln R between preset pairs gives Sub-Neptune->Neptunian -0.001, Neptunian->Saturnian -0.048, Jovian->Hot Jupiter -0.456 — the real sign is flat-to-NEGATIVE. Frozen carries the single largest ungated error, +84.6% at R=1.2. Gated-out classes keep exponent 1.0, i.e. the status quo: no regression, and the debt is DECLARED rather than silently papered over. compositionClass is importable without a cycle (e1Regime.js imports only alea + mathutil and never reads surfaceGravity).

SUB-EARTH BRANCH = piecewise in ABSOLUTE R with n_lo = 4/3, n_hi = 1.70, continuous at R = 1. Taken without asking, same rule. The handoff's implicit n_lo = 1.0 is the M -> 0 INCOMPRESSIBLE ASYMPTOTE, not the sub-Earth value: Valencia, O'Connell & Sasselov 2006 (arXiv:astro-ph/0511150, Icarus 181:545) Table 2 gives five fitted beta = 0.2991-0.3094 -> n = 1/beta - 2 = 1.23-1.34. n_lo = 1.0 would be wrong by ~33% in the exponent across the band where 8 of 13 rocky/icy presets live. HONESTY FLAG that must reach the code comment: Valencia's sub-Earth family is Super-MERCURIES (CMF 50/65/80%), so extrapolating to Earth's CMF 32.6% is OUR inference, not their result; the defensible bracket is n_lo in [1.23, 1.34] and 4/3 is its top end chosen for being exact and rational. Valencia's own framing is that the exponent falls TOWARD the constant-density value without reaching it — do not restate this as 'it is not 1.0'.

THE FORM STAYS THE NORMALIZED-AT-CANONICAL RATIO g = g_c * f(R)/f(R_c), with f piecewise in absolute Earth radii. NOT an absolute re-derivation from a Zeng M(R). This is load-bearing for byte-identity: f(R_c)/f(R_c) is x/x on the identical float = exactly 1.0, so g_c*1.0 === g_c bit-for-bit for any exponent. An absolute Zeng re-derivation gives g(1 R_E) = 0.99355 rather than 1.000 and would move all 75 carrier rows plus tests/worldengine-base-condition-vector.test.js:141. Measured, not argued: a matched control/mutation pair run under a scratchpad vitest config (repo untouched) held verify-golden 40c18aad and all 83 byte-identity test cases green.

THE RATIO-FORM TRAP IS WHY THE PIECEWISE MUST BE IN ABSOLUTE R, NOT A RATIO POWER. An anchored ratio and a piecewise-in-absolute-R law agree ONLY if R and R_c sit on the same branch. 8 of 13 rocky/icy presets have R_c < 1 (Moon/Mercury 0.38, Titan 0.40, Frozen 0.50, Europa 0.50, Mars 0.53, Crystal 0.80, Lava 0.90, Venus 0.95), so they never agree at any off-canonical radius. Carbon's ENTIRE draw band ['carbon': 0.4-0.9] sits below 1 despite R_c = 1.1.

REGISTER THE LAW BEFORE CHANGING THE CODE, so the registry is the falsification instrument rather than a rubber stamp. Verified red-then-green during grounding: the drafted measure against CURRENT code returns exponent 1.000 against a claimed 1.700. The registry's nullValue is 1.0 (the retired constant-density law), NOT 0 — 'g ignores radius' is not a state this code can reach, so a null of 0 guards nothing and a resolution-poor sweep would return a false PASS. Same construction as crater-count-independent-of-gravity, whose null is the removed g^0.34 coupling. Because the law is piecewise, register TWO entries (one per branch, each swept strictly inside its own validity band), not one with a hidden breakpoint.

THE EXPONENT IS COMPOSITION-BLIND WITHIN THE ROCKY CLASS, so no CMF / ironFraction plumbing is needed. Zeng's prefactor (1.07 - 0.21*CMF) enters g only as a multiplicative constant k^-3.7 and cancels identically in the normalized ratio form. Confirmed numerically: a CMF sweep 0->1 reproduces (R/R_c)^1.7 to <= 2e-15. radiusEarth is already the third argument to deriveConditionVector.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Spine conformance per Rule 15. (1) Driver connectivity: radiusEarth is already D-slot-backed and g_c comes from deriveBodyScalars (baseStep.js:20); the exponents 4/3 and 1.70 are the one new class of scalar and are LITERATURE CONSTANTS, not drivers, so each is declared as such with its source and validity band rather than being smuggled in as a tuned number. (2) Named consumer: no new emitted field, but the AC must state honestly that e1Regime.js:90-92 and giant-drivers.js:176 reconstruct M = g*R^2, so the mass law they see silently becomes M_c*(R/R_c)^3.7 on the rocky branch. (3) Taxonomy: N/A unless the exponent becomes a GUI knob or the composition gate becomes a selectable regime — declare it so explicitly. Plus the DOES/UNLOCKS card in intent.md.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Gravity on the drawn-radius axis obeys the self-compression law where the literature covers it: g = g_c * f(R)/f(R_c) with f(R) = R^(4/3) for R <= 1 and R^1.70 for R > 1, on the rocky class only. Two LAW_REGISTRY entries (one per branch) are registered in src/worldengine/instrument/laws.js BEFORE the code change and each is swept strictly inside its own validity band — the high branch inside R in [1.000, 1.754] (Zeng's 1-8 M_E at CMF 1/3), never across the R = 1 breakpoint, because a sweep that crosses the break measures the BLEND and not the law (measured during grounding: a [0.5 .. 4.0] sweep returns 1.507 +/- 0.070, which FAILS a claim of 1.70).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: MAX'S GATE ALONE — no agent drives or passes this. On a rocky world, does the planet read as GETTING HEAVIER as it gets bigger, in the way the surface tells you about the world? DISCLOSED CARVE-OUT, stated up front so Max is not sent looking for something that cannot happen: the GLOBAL relief amplitude will NOT move, because uPerturb is fed the canonical radius-blind gravity and reliefEnvelope discards its radius argument (see statusNote non-goal). If the honest answer is 'I cannot see any of this', that is a legitimate UAT outcome and it means the visible payoff is gated behind the uPerturb wiring fix, which would then be the next thing to scope.
